worldModelElicitationSessions.purpose: Converge ambiguous level-4 spatial requirements into a closed world model before World Model Review.

rawIntents.statement: The cube should roll up, down, left, right, forward, and backward in a way that feels consistent to the player.

modelHypotheses.name: Cube Local Control Frame
modelHypotheses.assumption: Input directions are interpreted relative to the cube's current local orientation.
modelHypotheses.predictionSummary: After rolling upward onto a wall, backward input follows the cube's transformed local frame.

modelHypotheses.name: Current Surface Control Frame
modelHypotheses.assumption: Input directions are interpreted relative to the surface the cube is currently contacting.
modelHypotheses.predictionSummary: After rolling onto a wall, left/right/up/down are remapped to the wall plane.

modelHypotheses.name: World XYZ Control Frame
modelHypotheses.assumption: Input directions are interpreted as absolute world axes.
modelHypotheses.predictionSummary: Backward always means negative world Z even when the camera uses a different visual frame.

modelHypotheses.name: Fixed Camera Control Frame
modelHypotheses.assumption: Input directions are interpreted from the fixed camera view and do not rotate with cube orientation or current surface.
modelHypotheses.predictionSummary: After up then backward, backward means visually backward from the fixed camera.

discriminatingQuestions.scenario: The cube rolls upward once, then receives a backward input.
discriminatingQuestions.questionText: After the cube moves up once, when the player presses backward, should it move backward as seen from the fixed camera, or backward relative to the cube/surface?

expectedAnswers.answerPattern: Backward from the fixed camera view.
Backward from the cube or current surface.

discriminatingQuestions.selectionRationale: This question separates fixed visual control from local, surface, and absolute-axis interpretations with one short state transition.
discriminatingQuestions.resultingModelUpdate: Select fixed camera control frame if answer follows visual backward.

humanAnswers.answerText: Fixed camera. Even after moving up, backward means backward from the camera view.
Up then up should keep climbing in the same visual up direction.
Up then down should reverse along the visual path.
Up then left should move left as seen from the fixed camera, not relative to the cube face.
Down, left, then down should still use the fixed camera control directions.
Up then backward should go visually backward from the fixed camera.
Yes, that rule is correct: control direction is fixed to the camera and does not change with cube orientation or surface.

hypothesisEliminations.rationale: The answer explicitly chooses fixed camera backward after a prior upward move.

counterexampleSequences.purpose: Check whether repeated movement remains visually stable after surface transition.
Check reversal semantics after the first transition.
Expose whether orthogonal movement is cube-relative or camera-relative.
Check composed transitions across multiple surfaces.
Expose the control reference frame directly.

sequenceExpectations.interpretation: Inverse movement is based on the fixed visual control frame.

sequenceExpectations.expectedOutcome: Each step follows fixed camera controls.
sequenceExpectations.interpretation: Composed transitions do not rotate the control frame.

sequenceExpectations.expectedOutcome: Backward means visually backward from the fixed camera.
sequenceExpectations.interpretation: Reference frame is fixed camera control.

invariantCandidates.statement: The control frame is fixed to the camera and does not change with physical cube orientation or current surface.
invariantCandidates.scope: Player directional input for cube rolling transitions.

invariantConfirmations.confirmationQuestion: Can we state the rule as: the control frame is fixed to the camera and never rotates with the cube or current surface?

derivedWorldModels.title: Fixed Camera Cube Rolling World Model
derivedWorldModels.summary: Directional inputs are interpreted from a fixed camera frame across repeated, inverse, orthogonal, reference-frame, and composed rolling transitions.

acceptanceScenarios.scenario: Given any cube orientation or current surface, directional input is applied in the fixed camera frame.
acceptanceScenarios.expectedResult: Up, down, left, right, forward, and backward produce visually consistent movement from the fixed camera perspective.

qualityIntentCandidates.statement: Cube control behavior must preserve fixed-camera directional consistency across surface transitions.
qualityIntentCandidates.lossBoundary: A player must not experience controls that change reference frame after the cube rolls onto a new surface.

elicitationClosureAssessments.rationale: All competing reference-frame hypotheses were resolved, the invariant was confirmed, and representative transition sequences were converted into an acceptance scenario.

semanticValidityRequires: expert review when domain risk requires it
